author: adityaksolves
body:
Related to #113054

**⚠️ Breaking Change:** Failed-file cleanup now requires explicit `failed_file_ttl_sec`
configuration; the previous implicit behavior (cleaning failed files whenever
`tracked_file_ttl_sec` was set) has been removed to provide independent control
over successful vs. failed file retention.

**Previous Behavior (master):** Setting `tracked_file_ttl_sec` implicitly enabled
TTL-based cleanup for both successfully processed files (`/processed` nodes) and
failed files (`/failed` nodes).

**New Behavior (this PR):** `tracked_file_ttl_sec` now cleans only `/processed`
nodes; `failed_file_ttl_sec` cleans only `/failed` nodes.

**Migration:** If your existing table relied on `tracked_file_ttl_sec` to also
clean up failed files, explicitly set `failed_file_ttl_sec` to the same value:
```sql
ALTER TABLE queue MODIFY SETTING failed_file_ttl_sec = 3600;
```

Check if your table is affected:
```sql
SELECT name, engine, create_table_query
FROM system.tables
WHERE engine LIKE '%S3Queue%'
  AND create_table_query LIKE '%tracked_file_ttl_sec%'
  AND create_table_query NOT LIKE '%failed_file_ttl_sec%';
```

Scope of this PR (Phase 1, as discussed in the issue):
- `failed_file_ttl_sec` setting (default: 0, disabled), reusing the existing cleanup thread and
  `cleanup_interval_min_ms`/`cleanup_interval_max_ms` cadence, following
  the same pattern as `tracked_file_ttl_sec`.
- `SYSTEM DROP S3QUEUE FAILED FILES db.table` for full, on-demand clearing
  of the failed set. Shares the same distributed lock as the periodic
  cleanup sweep to avoid races, and clears both Keeper znodes and the
  in-memory cache.
- Both features are restricted to **unordered mode only** in this PR;
  ordered mode support and `LIKE 'prefix/%'` pattern filtering are planned
  for a follow-up PR (Phase 2), per the scoping discussion in the issue.
- Documentation added for both the setting and the SYSTEM command.

Not closing #113054 with this PR since Phase 2 work remains.

### Changelog category
Backward Incompatible Change

### Changelog entry
Added `failed_file_ttl_sec` setting for S3Queue (unordered mode) to clean up
failed files from Keeper after a configurable TTL, and `SYSTEM DROP S3QUEUE
FAILED FILES` to manually clear them. Breaking change: failed-file cleanup now
requires explicit `failed_file_ttl_sec` configuration; the previous behavior
(cleaning failed files when `tracked_file_ttl_sec` was set) has been removed.
Tables with `tracked_file_ttl_sec` in unordered mode that relied on implicit
cleanup must set `failed_file_ttl_sec` explicitly.

### 💡 What
Added full keyboard accessibility to interactive custom `div` elements, specifically the `.gallery-item` (lightbox triggers) and `.bar-segment` (map modal triggers) components.

### 🎯 Why
These custom elements were previously only accessible via mouse clicks, breaking WCAG standards for keyboard accessibility. Users relying on a keyboard or assistive technologies could not focus these elements with `Tab` or trigger their actions with `Enter` or `Space`.

### 📸 Before/After
- **Before:** Elements were skipped by the keyboard focus order and didn't respond to keys.
- **After:** Elements receive keyboard focus naturally and execute their click logic when `Enter` or `Space` is pressed, without scrolling the page unnecessarily. (Screenshots and videos generated during verification step).

### ♿ Accessibility
- Added `tabindex="0"` to make the elements focusable.
- Added `role="button"` to inform screen readers of their interactive nature.
- Mapped `Enter` and `Space` keydowns to the element's existing `click()` logic.
- Prevented default page scrolling on `Space` press.
- Refrained from adding generic `aria-label` attributes to parent wrappers, preserving the rich descriptive content (like `alt` text) for screen readers.

author: xljones
body:
## Changes

Documents capture-group aliases on the path cleaning page. Until now the page described the alias as *"the replacement string for the matched portion of the URL"* and showed only fixed aliases, so there was no way to discover that an alias can reference the regex's capture groups.

Adds a **Reusing part of the matched URL** section to `contents/docs/_snippets/path-cleaning.mdx` (imported by both the Web Analytics and Product Analytics path cleaning pages, so one edit covers both) with:

- Two worked examples, each shown as a before/after table, where the capture group is genuinely load-bearing – grouping deep pages by section, and dropping a trailing fragment from paths of a given shape.
- The alias syntax table: `\1` to `\9`, `\0`, `\\`.
- The gotchas that actually bite: `$1` stays literal, there's no `\10`, PostHog rejects an out-of-range group reference on save, and JSON callers need the backslash doubled.
- When a capture group is worth its extra per-row cost.

The **Alias** bullet in "Configuring path cleaning rules" is also updated so it no longer implies the alias must be a fixed string, and a new line there spells out which value rules are matched against – a path for the web analytics tiles, but a full URL for a Paths insight or a URL breakdown. That distinction was missing, and it decides whether a leading `^/` anchor matches anything at all.

A **Matching both paths and full URLs** subsection then gives the way out: make the scheme and host an optional capture group. It also documents the trap, since simply dropping the `^` anchor doesn't fail loudly – the hostname gets counted as a path segment instead, so the rule quietly returns the wrong grouping.

## Why

Capture-group aliases shipped in PostHog/posthog#78193, which fixed the in-app previews, added save-time validation, and updated the in-app and MCP copy. Its own "Docs update" note flags this public page as the remaining follow-up. Without it, anyone whose routes share a shape still writes one rule per route instead of one rule for all of them.

Every example was verified by running the same replacement the query layer uses, rather than taken from the implementation on trust. That check is what caught the first draft's flagship example: it collapsed a locale prefix, which needs no capture group at all, because path cleaning only replaces the *matched* portion of the URL and a fixed alias already leaves the rest alone. Both forms produced byte-identical output, so the example taught the feature on a case that didn't need it. The section now leads with why a fixed alias is usually enough, then shows the cases where the text you want to keep differs on every row and only `\1` will do.

The new section was also checked with `markdownlint-cli2` and compiled through MDX v1 to confirm the backslashes survive the parse.

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the [docs](https://posthog.com/handbook/wizard-and-docs/docs-style-guide) and/or [content](https://posthog.com/handbook/content/posthog-style-guide) style guides.
- [x] Words are spelled using American English
- [x] Use relative URLs for internal links
- [ ] I've checked the pages added or changed in the Vercel preview build
- [x] If I moved a page, I added a redirect in `vercel.json` (n/a – no pages moved)

author: melbos
body:
A role stored without a `capabilities` key, or with a non-array value for it, causes two separate problems, not just one:

1. A fatal `TypeError` in `WP_User_Query::prepare_query()` when querying by capability, since `array_filter()` is called directly on `$role_data['capabilities']`. This is the crash originally reported on the ticket, via `wp_dropdown_users()` on the classic Author meta box.
2. The same unguarded assumption exists in `WP_Roles::init_roles()`, which runs on effectively every request that initializes roles — not just capability-filtered queries. Neither #8351 nor #8823 addresses this second call site.

This can happen when a plugin registers a role without capabilities and is later deactivated, leaving the malformed role behind in the site's `user_roles` option.

This PR builds on the investigation already done in #8351 (by @geekofshire) and #8823 (by @umeshnevase) — thank you both. It combines the `is_array()` robustness from #8823 with the more readable guard-clause shape from #8351, extends the same fix to `WP_Roles::init_roles()`, and adds the unit test coverage that @johnbillion asked for and that both prior PRs were still missing.

### Reproduction

Reproduced against a real WordPress install (not just the unit tests) by creating a role with no `capabilities` key and triggering the exact code path from the original report (`wp_dropdown_users()` with a capability filter):

**Before the fix** (`wp-content/debug.log`):
```
[07-Aug-2026 10:00:41 UTC] PHP Warning:  Undefined array key "capabilities" in wp-includes/class-wp-roles.php on line 310
[07-Aug-2026 10:00:41 UTC] PHP Warning:  Undefined array key "capabilities" in wp-includes/class-wp-roles.php on line 310
[07-Aug-2026 10:00:41 UTC] PHP Warning:  Undefined array key "capabilities" in wp-includes/class-wp-user-query.php on line 485
[07-Aug-2026 10:00:41 UTC] PHP Fatal error:  Uncaught TypeError: array_filter(): Argument #1 ($array) must be of type array, null given in wp-includes/class-wp-user-query.php:485
Stack trace:
#0 wp-includes/class-wp-user-query.php(485): array_filter(NULL)
#1 wp-includes/class-wp-user-query.php(79): WP_User_Query->prepare_query(Array)
#2 wp-includes/user.php(879): WP_User_Query->__construct(Array)
#3 wp-includes/user.php(1810): get_users(Array)
#4 ...: wp_dropdown_users(Array)
  thrown in wp-includes/class-wp-user-query.php on line 485
```

**After the fix**, same broken role, same trigger: no warnings, no errors, `debug.log` isn't even created, and the query returns results correctly instead of crashing.

### Testing

- Added two unit tests covering both failure modes (missing key, and a non-array value). Verified they fail at the correct line (`class-wp-user-query.php:485`, matching the original report) without the fix, and pass with it.
- Ran the full `user` and `capabilities` test groups (1,343 tests, 4,530 assertions) to confirm no regressions.
- Added a third test for the multisite network case: `WP_User_Query` doesn't need `switch_to_blog()` to query another site's users — it calls `WP_Roles::for_site( $blog_id )` directly, which reloads and re-initializes roles for that site in place. A role missing `capabilities` on a *different* site in the network hits the same unguarded code, so this exercises that path with the core test suite's multisite mode (`WP_TESTS_MULTISITE=1`). Verified it fails at `class-wp-roles.php:310` via `for_site()` without the fix, and passes with it. Ran the `user`/`capabilities`/`multisite` groups under multisite (763 tests, 3,137 assertions) to confirm no regressions there either. Details in `repro-evidence/multisite-verification.md`.

Trac ticket: https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/62600

## Use of AI Tools

AI assistance: Yes
Tool(s): Claude Code
Model(s): Claude Sonnet 5
Used for: Investigating the root cause (including finding the second, unreported crash site in `WP_Roles::init_roles()`), implementing the fix in both files, writing and running the unit tests, and reproducing the bug against a live WordPress install to verify the before/after behavior shown above. All changes were reviewed and directed by me.

# Changes

Test-hygiene chunk: quarantine hygiene. Every uncategorised `[Retry(3)]` in the Nethermind.* test projects is removed by fixing the underlying flake, and the one assert-inside-callback fixture is made unable to pass vacuously. The root-cause investigation also surfaced latent defects in the sync product code; they are fixed here, each in its own commit with a regression test (see "Product fixes" below).

Each Retry site was first classified with repeated local runs, then root-caused through git/PR archaeology, code tracing, and - for the one that resisted - an instrumented build that caught the failure in the act.

## Two shared levers behind six of the ten sites (`PayloadPreparationService`)

- **Payload cleanup eviction**: the test-local `ConfigurePayloadPreparationService` helper omitted `slotsPerOldPayloadCleanup`, silently re-enabling a cleanup that `MergeTestBlockchain` deliberately disables. At test slot lengths (40-500ms) the cleanup timer evicts the payload under test within milliseconds of a stall, and `getPayload` returns null - the exact `Is.Not.Null` flakes documented in #11881. The helper now keeps the 50k default.
- **Improvement-loop slot cutoff**: at `timePerSlot * 1.3` the service stops improving and no further improvement events fire, so every `WaitFor*` hangs to the 30s test timeout. One slow build was enough to trip it (`lastBuildTime` participates). `timePerSlot` is now 60s in the three tests that only use it as a lifetime bound, putting the cutoff beyond the test token. (`Cannot_produce_bad_blocks` keeps 40ms: it derives a random delay from `timePerSlot.Milliseconds`, which breaks at >= 1s.)

## Per-test changes

- `getPayloadV1_waits_for_block_production`: asserted a transaction-count *rate band* (0.5x-2x) between two independently scheduled parties (a `Thread.Sleep`-paced tx source vs the test thread's `Task.Delay`), with a mis-modelled expectation sitting one tick below its upper bound. The tx source now blocks on a semaphore with a per-case permit count and aborts on the production token (published through a new factory callback); the three cases assert exact counts (50 / 5 / 0). The partial case cancels the blocked pull through `getPayload` and reads the settled block through a bounded poll on a second read, because requiring the cancelled build to finish inside `getPayload`'s 50ms non-empty wait is a wall-clock cliff - review reproduced 5/5 failures under full-core CPU load with the naive shape, and the final shape runs 15/15 green under the same saturation. `[Parallelizable(ParallelScope.None)]` is no longer needed (suite time 13s -> 4s).
- `consecutive_blockImprovements_should_be_disposed`: four hazards - unsynchronised reads of the factory's `CreatedContexts` list, a dispose-ordering window, the slot cutoff, and a timed background tx writer. Now: an increment-on-read counter replaces the writer, reads go through a locked snapshot accessor, the disposal asserts target the two oldest (provably superseded) contexts, and the test freezes the counter and waits for the context count to settle before `getPayload` - a live improvement chain races retrieval, and a context created in that window is never disposed (found empirically; the old test dodged it only because the cutoff had already killed the chain).
- `getPayloadV1_picks_transactions_from_pool_constantly_improving_blocks`: waited on *any* improvement per round, so a mid-batch wake produced `[3,4,11]` and broke the equality. Each round now waits for the improvement that contains its full batch; the sequence assert allows intermediate steps (`Is.Ordered` + superset of `{3,6,11}`).
- `TestTwoTransaction_SameContract_WithBlockImprovement`: slot-cutoff victim only (a large contract deploy in round 1 could trip the cutoff and round 2 never started); fixed by the lever fixes alone.
- `getPayloadV1_does_not_wait_for_improvement_when_block_is_not_empty`: same - both hazards were the levers; the waits were already event-driven.
- `Cannot_produce_bad_blocks`: its `Is.Not.Null` flakes were pure cleanup-eviction (#11881 documented the mechanism); with the lever fixed the Retry is dropped. **The Retry here was actively dangerous**: it guarded the `PayloadStatus.Valid` consensus assert, so a genuine bad-block race would have been retried into green. The diagnostic log sweep now only runs when logging is enabled (it referenced a hardcoded `D:\logs` path that does not exist on CI, turning a real failure into `DirectoryNotFoundException`).
- `Maintain_correct_pointers_for_beacon_sync_in_archive_sync`: `IsBeaconSyncFinished` flips on `WasProcessed`, which the main-chain update sets *after* both waits the test already performed; a 1s re-submitting poll bridged the gap and added queue backlog per retry. The test now awaits `BlockAddedToMain` for the best beacon block and submits the payload once.
- `Peer_sends_just_one_item_when_advertising_more_blocks_but_no_bodies`: #11850 fixed the cause (a racy `AutoResetEvent` peer gate) and deleted the Retry; #11937 (a mechanical `long`->`ulong` refactor) re-added it on the conflicting lines. Dropped again; the download path is synchronous end to end.
- `Can_reorg_based_on_total_difficulty` + `Can_extend_chain_on_new_block_when_high_difficulty_low_number` (one root cause, in the test harness): `SyncingContext.AllInstances` was a process-wide **static** queue, and every fixture instance's `[OneTimeTearDown]` stopped every context in it with no ownership check. The six parameterized fixture instances run in parallel, so the first instance to finish both tests disposed other instances' still-live containers mid-test; the victim's wait then ran out its full 60s because its synchronizer was already stopped. Only a multi-test filter (or the full suite) exposes this: teardown cannot run until a fixture finishes all its selected tests, so single-test runs stay phase-aligned and tear down after every gate has fired - which is why 50x single-test repeats never caught what CI's full suite hit. Root-caused with an instrumented build that captured the foreign `StopAsync` in the act (context killed 2ms after suggesting the reorg branch, gate then dead-waited 60s); the same instrumentation refuted the peer-allocation and thread-pool-starvation hypotheses (a misdirected bodies allocation self-heals in ~0.1ms). Master with the two retries stripped fails the same way (2/10 runs), so the flake predates this PR - the static registry dates to the original parallel-sync work and predates #11881's Retry. The registry is now owned per fixture instance and drained by a per-test `[TearDown]`, which also stops a failed test from leaking a hot container into the next test (previously a failing assert skipped the fluent chain's trailing `StopAsync`, so **each Retry attempt ran against the leaked containers of the previous one**). Both tests additionally arm a `NewSuggestedBlock` gate before adding peerB (event-driven and fail-fast; `NewBestSuggestedBlock` does not fire for the fast fixtures) and dispose via `await using`. The extend test's tail now adds block 7 - re-adding block 6 was a no-op, so its final assert could not fail.

body:
## What

Closes the **code half of D5**. Every tool call is now decided against the deployment policy (ADR-0041, NFR-SEC-49).

## Placement, and why it is tested on source order

The gate sits **between the tool-name allowlist and the resolve step**:

- **after** the allowlist, so a policy rule is never consulted for a name the gateway does not serve
- **before** the serializer and the forward, so a denied call acquires no session slot and Control materializes nothing for a call it must never execute

"No session exists for a denied call" is not observable from a unit test after the fact, so the ordering is asserted on the **source order of the real call sites**. The anchors are call sites, not comments — a comment can move without the code it describes, leaving the test agreeing with a handler that no longer does what it says.

## Argument extraction

`toolArgumentsFrom` decodes **one level, strings only**. The policy's sole argument predicate reads a top-level string, so decoding deeper would build a surface the policy cannot express. A number or object is carried as `nil`, so the evaluator sees *unreadable* rather than a coerced stand-in.

An unreadable body yields an **empty map**, which `Decide` refuses for any tool carrying a predicate. Inventing an argument the caller never sent would decide the call on fabricated input.

## Binding, and the failure direction

The policy binds through `WithPolicy` rather than a ninth constructor parameter: it is the one seam a *deployment* supplies as a document. A boot that skips the bind leaves a handler whose **zero Policy denies everything** — visible at once, rather than as a permissive surface.

A configured policy path that cannot be read or does not validate **fails boot**. Falling back to the baseline would run a surface the operator did not choose while they believed their file was in force.

## The baseline is permissive, and tested to stay so

A test asserts it grants **every advertised tool**. The baseline exists to reproduce today's behaviour as an auditable rule set, so a tool the gateway serves but the baseline omits would be a silent narrowing on upgrade.

## Test fallout, stated plainly

Every test builder now binds the baseline, because the zero Policy denies by design. One test sent **empty arguments** to the file verbs and was denied for a reason unrelated to what it asks — it now sends a path inside a granted prefix, since it is about the *name* allowlist not regressing.

## Mutation — four mutants

gate removed · verdict ignored · empty argument set passed · extractor fabricating an argument

**"Verdict ignored" survived the first pass.** The source-order test proves *where* the gate sits, not that it has an **effect** — and the permissive baseline allows the calls every other test makes. A behavioural test now asserts a denied call is refused and never reaches the forward.

## What changed

Deleted one of two identical `usePermissions` entries in the `vi.mock("@/hooks", ...)`
factory of `frontend/src/components/chat/chat-model-picker.test.tsx`.

That was enough to make `bun run type-check` exit 0 on `main`. Until now it failed:

```
src/components/chat/chat-model-picker.test.tsx(37,3): error TS1117:
An object literal cannot have multiple properties with the same name.
```

`make lint-frontend` runs `tsc`, and so does CI's `test-frontend` job, so this was red
on every branch cut from `main` — including the four open ones.

## Why nothing caught it

The second entry wins at runtime and its body is identical to the first, so it changed
no behaviour: the suite is green with the duplicate and green without it, same 16
tests. `bun run test:run` and `bun run test:coverage` both pass on this file either
way. `tsc` was the only gate that could see it, and it is not part of "I ran the tests
and they were green" — which is the shape #487 names, and the same one behind #476.

## The issue's attribution is wrong, and the real story is worth recording

#487 blames #360 (`8a6ba58`). That commit touched this file, but only to rewrite two
assertion strings — `git show 8a6ba58 -- <file>` is four lines, none of them in the
mock factory.

It is two pull requests landing the same mock entry a day apart, neither seeing the
other:

- **#433** (`3254969`, *check secrets:edit inside the inline secret form*) appended
  `usePermissions` after `useSecrets`.
- **#442** (`63f250b`, *check the permission before offering the write*) added it again
  in alphabetical position, between `useModelProviders` and `useProviderModels`.

`chat-model-picker.test.tsx` is the only source file both touched. That is why this
happened here and nowhere else, and it is a plain merge collision rather than a
copy-paste inside one edit.

**#442's is the one kept**, because its position preserves the factory's alphabetical
order.

## How it was verified

- `cd frontend && bun run type-check` — exits 0, no output.
- `bunx vitest run src/components/chat/chat-model-picker.test.tsx
  src/components/chat/chat-model-picker.integration.test.tsx` — 2 files, 16 tests,
  passed. Unchanged from before, as expected: the deleted entry never ran.
- **Checked for the same shape elsewhere, two ways.** `tsc` reporting nothing else is
  itself the repo-wide answer for duplicate keys — TS1117 is raised per object
  literal, so a second occurrence anywhere would still be in that output. And for the
  shape `tsc` *cannot* see — two separate `vi.mock` calls naming the same module,
  where the second silently replaces the first — a scan over every test file in
  `frontend/src` found no module mocked twice.

Frontend-only and test-only, so no page under `docs/` describes anything this changes.

Closes #487

author: elecmonkey
body:
## Summary

Port `eslint-plugin-jest`'s `expect-expect` to rstest: every test registration must contain at least one assertion, otherwise the test can pass without verifying anything. Added to the rstest `recommended` preset at `warn`, matching `jest/expect-expect`.

The framework-neutral ledger is extracted into a shared body under `internal/utils/test_framework/rules/expect_expect`; `jest/expect-expect` becomes a thin wrapper over it.

## Behavior change in `jest/expect-expect`

Extracting the shared body also fixes one order-dependent false positive in `jest/expect-expect`. For a named callback whose declaration is asserting, the registration is now treated as covered **regardless of source order**:

```js
function myTest() {
  expect(true).toBeDefined();
}
it('should fail', myTest);
```

Upstream `eslint-plugin-jest` reports `Test has no assertions` here because the assertion is walked before the `it(...)` registration is queued; the shared engine instead records the asserting declaration and clears the registration whenever it is seen. Since the function declaration is hoisted, this snippet is runtime-equivalent to the call-first form (`it(...); function myTest() { ... }`) that both implementations already accept, so treating the two identically is the correct behavior. The previously-invalid case is now a valid test case, and the divergence is documented in the rule doc.

## Differences from jest

rstest's assertion API is vitest/chai lineage, so the wrapper diverges from jest where the framework differs:

- **default `assertFunctionNames` is `["expect", "assert"]`** — rstest exposes both as globals; no `expectTypeOf` / `bench` handling, since rstest core has neither.
- **assertions are recognized through the shared rstest call analysis, not by callee text alone** — `context.expect(...)`, `rstest.expect(...)`, an aliased `import { expect as check }` and `import.meta.rstest.expect(...)` all count without configuration, matching what `rstest/no-conditional-expect` already recognizes.
- **the `.todo` exemption reads the semantic `ParsedRstestFnCall.Todo` field**, which survives const aliases (`const t = test.todo; t('x')`), rather than the call-site `Members`.
- **test registrations are resolved through the shared rstest call analysis (`GetRstestCallAnalysis` / `ParseFnCall`)**, covering `import.meta.rstest`, `test.extend`, `.each` / `.for`, and `@rstest/playwright`.

author: rbuergi
body:
## Summary

Fixes #697 — removed users kept reading protected data until the portal restarted.

**Mechanism.** `PostgreSqlPartitionedMeshQuery.FanOutQuery` was **one-shot by design**: a single `Initial`, then complete, with no change-feed subscription (its class doc declared *"live deltas across partitions are out of scope"*). `PermissionEvaluator.ObserveAllMembershipNodes` opens a **path-less** query (`nodeType:GroupMembership scope:subtree`) — path-less deliberately, because a group and its members can live in a different partition than the grant. On partitioned PG a path-less query pins to no partition, so **all three providers went silent**: the fan-out completed after its Initial, the pedestrian deferred to the native provider on an empty path, the static provider completed. With no live subscription anywhere, the process-wide `Replay(1)` snapshot behind `IMeshNodeStreamCache.GetQuery` froze at its Initial **for the life of the process**.

Revocation only ever *appeared* to work via `SyncedQueryMeshNodes`' un-gated `Deleted` fast-path — which several delete routes bypass, and which has no Created/Updated counterpart. That is exactly why the reporter saw re-creating a membership have no live effect either: it failed in **both** directions.

The same freeze silently affected **every** path-less security query — `$security-roles` and the **root** `$security-policy`.

**Family:** a third, *distinct* member. #868 and #889 were equality/dedup/deserialization gaps **on** a live path; here there was **no live source at all**. The fix composes with both — the `Added` it now emits relies on #889's duplicate-`Added` pass-through.

## The fix

`FanOutQuery` now honours the Initial-then-deltas contract: subscribes `MergedChanges`, buffers pre-Initial notifications (the same race-fix its two siblings already carry), re-queries serialised via `Concat`, diffs into `Added`/`Updated`/`Removed`.

Cost is bounded by an **exact relevance gate, not a debounce** — a path-less query's path/scope predicate matches *every* notification, so a naive re-query would run a cross-schema UNION per write. In order: a path already in the result set is relevant; otherwise a `Deleted` is not (a delete can only remove something we don't hold — which also makes the null-`Entity` delete payload a non-problem); otherwise the framework's own `QueryEvaluator.Matches` decides; unclassifiable re-queries. **Erring toward over-notifying is deliberate: under-notifying is a security hole, over-notifying costs one query.** `livePaths` is an `ImmutableHashSet` swapped wholesale under `Volatile`, so the hot filter takes no lock. No async/await outside the existing `IIoPool` leaf, no `FromAsync`, no statics.

## Verification

**Fail-without** (src reverted, rebuilt, re-run): both new tests fail — the query reported *"Last of **1** emission(s) was: ChangeType = Initial"* and nothing ever again; the evaluator folded once to `None` and never re-folded. **Pass-with:** 2/2.

Regression: full `MeshWeaver.Hosting.PostgreSql.Test` **641 passed / 1 skipped**, `MeshWeaver.Security.Test` **345 passed**, `AccessRestriction*` **14 passed**. Independently re-verified after merging current main: **12/12** across the new class + `EffectivePermissionPostgresTest` + `PaywallRealGateShapeTests`. `-c Release -warnaserror` clean.

## Residual risks (documented, not hidden)

- `FanOutQuery` no longer completes. Consumers use `.Where(Initial).Take(1)`, and the per-schema delegate serving every *scoped* query already never completed, so nothing could depend on completion — grepped for terminal `ToList()`/`LastAsync`/`Aggregate` on query streams, none found; full PG suite confirms.
- A path-less query with no filter and no text search still makes the gate always-true → a cross-schema re-query per write. No long-lived subscriber of that shape exists today, and it was previously *frozen* (equally broken), but the gate does not bound it.
- Text/vector fan-out relevance uses the in-memory matcher, which can be narrower than PG's HNSW vector match — strictly better than no liveness, not exact.
- Third copy of the snapshot-diff + `ItemEquals` logic; flagged in the XML doc as a consolidation candidate. Deliberately **not** refactored — the other two are the #849/#853/#868/#889 flake-sensitive paths.

No What's New entry: security fix; the user-visible effect (revocation takes effect immediately) rides the fix.

author: fresolina
body:
Five defects found while inspecting Sponza after the directional (cubed) irradiance work, across both read paths.

Un-voxelized surfaces took full sun. In directional modes the Baked shadow resolves through the SSBO face-plane loop, which only reads SOLID taps. Small protruding detail the conservative raster missed (a lion's nose, a brazier rim) skipped all four taps, leaving wsum at 0 and shadow at its 1.0 initialiser - full unshadowed sun inside an interior, blown out to flat white. Fall back to the air-layer alpha instead of assuming lit.

Cube read jumped a whole cell where the dominant normal axis changed. All three buckets shared one plane picked by the largest normal component, so carved geometry banded wherever the normal swept through a dominance boundary. Offset each bucket along its OWN axis instead: at a component's zero crossing the offset and the slab both flip, but n^2 is exactly 0 there, so it is continuous. Still three taps.

Single had the same snap. Replaced with a continuous offset (normal / max|n|) that keeps the guarantee the snap was there for - the dominant axis clears a full cell - without the discontinuity. Still one tap. Also fixes Single reading too dark on curved detail, where the snap was sampling occluded planes.

Cube shell dilation was direction-blind. It gated the 26-neighbour walk by the voxel's stored normal and wrote one average into every bucket, so two-sided voxels had no "front" to pick and bailed out to black. Each bucket now takes only the air on its own side, cosine-weighted, which removes the bail-out: a sub-voxel wall's two faces get different values from the same cell, so Cube no longer needs walls two voxels thick.

Baked sun shadow was blocky in directional modes. The face read is per-voxel quantised and samples _Radiance[].w raw, bypassing both the sun-visibility blur and ShadowSharpness. Cube now carries each face's visibility in the slab pointing that way and reads it n^2- weighted from the texture - per-side correct AND smooth, at three sampler taps instead of ~12 structured-buffer loads. TwoSided takes the texture path too except on genuinely two-sided voxels, which still need the face read.

### Motivation

- Provide a clean, auditable starting point for a `gpt-5.6`-only prompt-learning series by preserving legacy generated artifacts and preventing accidental gold leakage into model prompts. 
- Harden the segmentation/MWE pipeline and manual editor against common model/output problems (temperature rejection, whitespace-token annotation leaks, and UI error visibility). 
- Add interactive review and archival primitives to support the experiment workflow (archive initial outputs, freeze corrected segmentation, review prompt divergences, and iterative prompt improvement).

### Description

- Introduced a 5.6-only experiment namespace and archive workflow: new Makefile variables and targets such as `EXPERIMENT_SERIES`, `MODEL`, `archive-pre-5-6`, `refresh-segmentation-phase-2`, `archive-initial-segmentation-phase-2`, and `archive-corrected-segmentation-phase-2` to preserve old `generated/` data and drive a reproducible `gpt-5.6` prompt-learning loop. 
- Updated runners and management commands to accept an explicit `--model` and to stop passing `temperature=0` to newer GPT models, and prevented gold leakage by restricting model-facing input (e.g., `model_input_record` in chunk runner and removal of gold fields from prompts). 
- Added interactive review and archival management commands: `archive_segmentation_phase_2_outputs`, `review_mwe_prompt_divergences`, and improvements to `run_mwe_prompt_experiment`, `run_mwe_reconcile_prompt_experiment`, `run_chunk_prompt_on_corpus`, `evaluate_segmentation_outputs_with_ai`, and `prepare_chunk_prompt_improvement` to support model selection, review logging, and dry-run behavior. 
- Implemented token-level cleanup utilities and usage: new `src/pipeline/token_annotations.py` with `strip_whitespace_token_annotations` and its integration in `mwe`, `lemma`, and `gloss` pipelines and the page-oriented manual views; this removes spurious linguistic annotations on whitespace-only tokens and avoids MWE/lemma/gloss inconsistency. 
- Added corpus extraction extensions to `extract_chunk_segmentation_corpus` to allow explicitly assigning an allowlisted set of projects into a single split (`--selected-projects-split`) and a helper `prepare-seven-en-development-gold` in the segmentation Makefile to freeze selected projects as development gold. 
- UX and template tweaks: make error messages visually prominent in `projects/base.html` and adjust the manual segmentation save/validation logic to permit empty segments while preserving correct validation semantics. 
- Documentation and experiment artifacts: updated roadmap docs and README content to describe the reset/runbook and added a preliminary ALTA 2026 notes file capturing early GPT-5.6 results and protocol. 

### Testing

- Ran the updated Django/unit test suite covering `platform_server/projects` command tests and pipeline unit tests including `test_extract_chunk_segmentation_corpus`, `test_run_chunk_prompt_on_corpus`, `test_prepare_chunk_prompt_improvement`, `test_review_mwe_prompt_divergences`, and unit tests for MWE/lemma/gloss (`test_06_mwe.py`, `test_07_lemma.py`, `test_08_gloss.py`), and all modified tests passed. 
- Exercised end-to-end experiment flows in Makefiles via dry-run paths for `archive-pre-5-6`, `refresh-segmentation-phase-2` and `mwe-prompt-cycle` targets to validate argument plumbing and manifest outputs. 
- Verified model-interaction safety fixes by unit tests that assert prompt-building omits gold fields and by mocking AI clients to confirm that `temperature` is no longer passed in API calls.

A silent proxy or mirror that accepted the connection and sent response headers but then went quiet mid-body could hang a build indefinitely: the shared secure HTTP client set no read deadline, so `io.Copy` on the response body blocked forever, the 3-attempt retry loop never advanced, and the whole build wedged with no error (observed as ~11MB received, then a dead-but-`ESTABLISHED` socket to the proxy).

This PR adds two independent guards to the package fetcher:

- **`ResponseHeaderTimeout` (30s)** on the secure HTTP transport — covers the "connection up but no response headers" stall. Applied in both `GetSecureHTTPClient` (singleton) and `NewSecureHTTPClient`, so every caller (pkgfetcher, rpmutils, debutils, overlay, apt_sources) enforces the guard consistently.
- **`idleTimeoutReader` (60s idle window)** wrapping the response body — covers the mid-body stall. The timer resets on every read that returns bytes, so a slow-but-progressing large package download is never killed; only a true stall trips it. A trip surfaces as a copy error (wrapping the underlying cause), which removes the partial file and feeds the existing retry loop.

A flat `http.Client.Timeout` was intentionally avoided: it would cap total transfer time and could kill a legitimately large package on a slow link.

**Files changed**
- `internal/utils/network/securehttp.go` — add `ResponseHeaderTimeout` to both client constructors.
- `internal/ospackage/pkgfetcher/pkgfetcher.go` — wrap the response body in `idleTimeoutReader`.
- `internal/ospackage/pkgfetcher/pkgfetcher_test.go` — coverage for the stall/idle-timeout behavior and the slow-progress path.

#### Any Newly Introduced Dependencies

None. Uses only the Go standard library (`net/http`, `time`, `io`).

#### How Has This Been Tested? <!-- REQUIRED -->

- `go test ./internal/ospackage/pkgfetcher/... ./internal/utils/network/...` — tests simulate a mid-body stall (body goes silent after some bytes) and assert the fetch aborts with a "stalled" error, and confirm a slow-but-progressing download (chunks paced well under the idle window) is never killed.
- `go build ./...` and `golangci-lint run` on the affected packages.

author: jegertabt
body:
## Summary

Stabilizes bounded Stage 1 authorization checksums so continued intake outside an unchanged selected cohort does not alter that cohort's authorization identity.

## Proven production regression

Two read-only Scrypt generations for coin_id 1267 used selection_limit 25 and selected the same block IDs (20381 through 20405). Their projected block mutations and projected earning rows were canonically identical, but later eligible backlog growth from 401 to 419 candidates changed selection_checksum, intended_mutation_checksum, package_checksum, and report_checksum.

The cause was snapshot-wide reporting metadata in the selection payload and repeated snapshot-wide counts in the package payload. Later unselected candidates therefore contaminated checksums described as authorizing only the bounded cohort and its intended mutations.

## Repair

The v3 generator and validator now use the same shared canonicalization methods.

- selection_checksum binds coin_id, deterministic selection order, selected block IDs, and selected-cohort identity records: block_id, height, time, blockhash, userid, workerid, and current_category.
- intended_mutation_checksum binds coin_id, the stabilized selection checksum, complete projected block mutations, complete projected earning rows, canonical recipient totals, projected total amount, and approval_status.
- package_checksum binds schema, package type, command, coin/algo scope, selection limit and selected count, internal batch size and projected batch count, projected row/recipient counts and total, approval_status, both stabilized checksums, the structured apply command/options/shape, and the Stage 1-only pipeline boundary.
- report_checksum remains free to cover snapshot-wide reporting metadata, including eligible population, selection-limit exclusions, and the maximum eligible snapshot order key.

The v3 authorization payload no longer includes the full snapshot boundary, eligible_candidate_count, excluded_by_selection_limit_count, or excluded_newer_candidate_count. Those fields remain present and validated as report/snapshot metadata, but they cannot expand apply scope: apply still consumes only the exact selected IDs and projections bound by the stabilized checksums.

## Compatibility and safety

- Schema remains badpool.stage1_drain_manifest.v3.
- Authentic v2 manifests continue to validate with the exact deployed legacy v2 checksum payload.
- v2/v3 hybrid rejection remains intact.
- Exact package-checksum and exact confirmation validation remain intact.
- Bounded selection, deterministic ordering, post-snapshot exclusion, projection reverification, resumable progress, and Stage 1-only pipeline boundaries remain intact.
- No mutation semantics, CLI option names, or invocation shapes changed.
- No apply validation was weakened; v3 now additionally binds the structured apply contract and pipeline boundary inside package_checksum.

## Tests

PASS under PHP 8.5.8 WASM:

- badpool_stage1_checksum_stability_harness.php
- badpool_stage1_manifest_contract_harness.php
- badpool_stage1_drain_guard_harness.php
- badpool_stage1_apply_guard_harness.php

- badpool_approval_package_generator_harness.php

- badpool_operator_safety_contract_harness.php
- badpool_status_runner_guard_harness.php
- badpool_account_credit_guard_harness.php
- badpool_guardrail_report_parser_hardening_harness.php
- badpool_payout_row_apply_guard_harness.php
- badpool_wallet_proof_closeout_guard_harness.php
- badpool_wallet_send_apply_guard_harness.php
- badpool_wallet_send_dryrun_guard_harness.php
- block_path_diag_harness.php
- sha256d_version_rolling_replay.php

PHP syntax checks passed for all three modified PHP files. git diff --check passed.

The new regression generates populations of 401 and 419 candidates with the same bounded 25-block cohort and identical projections. It proves stable selection, intended-mutation, and package checksums; a differing report checksum; unchanged apply scope; Generation B self-authorization acceptance; and rejection against prior authorization after changing either one selected block or one intended amount.

Environment limitation: the native backend_entrypoint_guard_harness.php was not run because this runtime has no PCNTL extension.

## Remaining production verification

After review, merge, and a separately authorized deployment:

1. Run the native PCNTL backend entrypoint harness and the focused Stage 1 harnesses in the deployment environment.
2. Generate two read-only bounded Scrypt plan/package views while intake continues, without applying either.
3. Confirm identical selected IDs and projected mutation payloads produce identical selection_checksum, intended_mutation_checksum, and package_checksum while report_checksum and backlog metadata may differ.
4. Preserve the evidence artifacts and require separate operator review before any new authorization package or Stage 1 apply.

## What

A new **🔴 Live coach** mode that turns a round into targeted watchlist entries — **entirely offline. No AI, no account, no network, no cost.** Nothing leaves the device.

The "intelligence" is the app's curated tell database plus your own review — which is how GeoGuessr players actually train.

## Flow

1. **Capture** the round:
   - **🖥️ Watch my screen** — desktop browsers, via screen-share (`getDisplayMedia`); samples a frame every few seconds.
   - **📹 Upload a screen recording** — works on **iPhone**: record with Control Center, hand the app the video, it extracts frames. (Browsers can't silently watch another app, and live screen-share isn't available on iOS Safari — hence the upload route.)
2. **Name the country** you were in (the game reveals it at round end) — searchable picker.
3. **Tick the tells you noticed** from that country's full tell sheet.
4. **Debrief:** a score (e.g. 2/6), the tells you *missed* listed out, and those tells added to your ⭐ watchlist so they surface before your next round. Jump straight to the country's study page from there.

Frames are only ever drawn to a local canvas and shown back to you.

## History of this PR

It originally proposed an API-based AI vision coach; the second commit replaces that entirely with the offline self-review after the requester asked to avoid APIs. The capture/frame-extraction plumbing is reused; the Anthropic request, API-key/model UI, and the browser-direct-access call are all removed.

## Files (within the existing app — no new files)

- `index.html` — coach screen (capture + review), home button
- `style.css` — coach styles (frame strip, checklist, spinner)
- `app.js` — capture (live + upload), frame extraction, and the offline pick → checklist → missed-tells review
- `sw.js` — cache bumped to `geo-tells-v3`
- `README.md` — Live coach section

## Testing

- `node --check` on `app.js`
- Headless-browser run of the full offline flow with `getDisplayMedia` stubbed by a live canvas stream: verified a real frame is captured and shown in the strip, the country picker filters, the checklist lists the country's tells, ticking some yields the right score, unticked tells are listed as missed and written to the watchlist, and **the Anthropic endpoint is never contacted** (a route interceptor confirmed zero calls). No console errors beyond the expected `file://` service-worker warning.

author: botbikamordehai2-sketch
body:
## What
This fixes a regression where a `pltpu.sync_copy` (or `make_async_copy`) out of an HBM operand silently returns all zeros when the `pallas_call` has an additional operand that the kernel never reads, and that operand is produced inside the `jax.jit`. The bug appears on libtpu 0.0.43+ but not on 0.0.41. The issue requires the unused operand to be at least 4 rows of 128 lanes, source rows at least 256 floats wide, and a DMA of a strict sub-slice of an HBM operand into VMEM scratch.

## Fix
The root cause is in the Mosaic-TPU lowering: when an operand is unused, the lowering still assigns an address to it, but if the operand is created inside the jit, its buffer may not be properly allocated (or its address is zero), causing subsequent operand addresses to be computed incorrectly, leading to DMA reads from the wrong HBM location (hence zeros). The fix is to filter out unused operands from the `in_specs` in the lowering rule, so that they do not affect the addressing of other operands. This is done by detecting operands that are never accessed by the kernel (based on the Pallas indexing analysis) and removing their entries from the argument list before constructing the Mosaic computation.

Closes #39744

author: fantomasa
body:
## Summary

Fixes the intermittent failure of the `one-shot-single-minimal: verify deployment port-forwards stop` E2E test reported in #5735.

## Root cause

`verifyStopPortForwards` unconditionally asserted that `solo deployment port-forwards stop` prints `Stopped:`. The command only prints that line when at least one port-forward is configured; with zero configured it prints `No port-forwards configured in this deployment` instead.

Zero configured port-forwards is a **legitimate state**, not a bug: when one-shot creates its own Kind cluster, services are exposed via stable NodePort mappings and no port-forwards are registered in the remote config. When the cluster pre-exists (e.g. CI creates it via `setup-dual-e2e.sh`), one-shot falls back to the legacy kubectl port-forwards. Which path a run takes depends on the environment, which is why the failure is intermittent. The sibling `verifyDeploymentConfigPorts` test already branches on this same `No port-forwards configured` signal; this test did not, so it failed whenever the run took the NodePort path.

## Fix

Branch the assertion on the same signal the command emits, mirroring the established `verifyDeploymentConfigPorts` pattern:

- NodePort path (zero configured) → assert `Stopped:` is **absent**.
- Port-forward path → assert `Stopped:` is **present**.

The `Stopping Port-Forwards` header and the post-stop `config ports` "no port-forwards" assertion hold in both modes and are unchanged.

## Base branch

Targets `03286-stop-port-forward-command` rather than `main` because the `stopPortForwards` command and its test only exist on PR #5145; there is nothing to fix on `main` yet. This lands the fix into #5145 before it reaches `main`.

Fixes #5735

author: jsboigeepita
body:
## #1664 — le garde canonique couvrait un conteneur sur sept

`sanitize_state` se déclare « **the UNIQUE export guard** […] the single chokepoint through which a state snapshot must pass before reaching **git, a dashboard, a PR, or an API** ». Il opacifiait `dung_frameworks.arguments` en `f74d51a7` et laissait **mot pour mot** la même chaîne dans six conteneurs frères.

Cause : `dung_frameworks` est `Dict[str, Dict]`, ses frères sont `List[Dict]` remplis par `.append()`. Les passes 4b/4c écrites pour Dung sont gardées `isinstance(data[field], dict)` — inatteignables pour eux, sans trace.

## Ce qui est corrigé, et pourquoi ces champs-là

Le fil conducteur est `_extract_arguments_from_context` — l'helper que le commentaire de la passe 4b cite **lui-même** comme celui qui « puts the real claim text into `arguments` » pour justifier son existence. Il alimente **17 callables**, pas seulement Dung. Les writers stockent la liste verbatim, donc ces sous-clés portent du texte de revendication **par construction**, pas par hypothèse :

| Conteneur | Sous-clés | Jumeau Dung déjà couvert |
|---|---|---|
| `ranking_results` | `arguments` | `dung_frameworks.arguments` |
| `probabilistic_results` | `arguments`, **les clés de** `acceptance_probabilities` | le producteur écrit `{a: 0.5 for a in args}` — la map est **indexée par le texte** |
| `bipolar_results` | `arguments`, `supports` | `supports` a la forme exacte de `attacks` |
| `aspic_results` | `extensions` | forme exacte de `dung_frameworks[*].extensions` |
| `belief_revision_results` | `original`, `revised` | — |
| `dialogue_results` | `topic`, `trace[*].{argument,target}` | le writer journalise `topic[:50]`, donc le suppose long |
| `debate_transcripts` | `exchanges[*].{proponent_move,opponent_move}` | voir ci-dessous |

Le cas `debate_transcripts` est d'une autre nature : `_TEXT_STRIP_LISTS` **déclarait déjà** `proponent_move` et `opponent_move`, mais le vrai writer les niche un niveau plus bas dans `exchanges`. Deux des trois sous-clés déclarées n'ont jamais eu de cible. Ce commit complète une intention déjà enregistrée — il n'en ajoute pas une nouvelle.

## Anti-pendule — ce qui est délibérément laissé intact

Le contrat promet de **préserver** les agrégats structurels, et l'erreur symétrique serait de tout scrubber.

- **Étiquettes à vocabulaire fermé** : `ranking_results.method`, `aspic_results.reasoner_type`, `bipolar_results.framework_type`, `belief_revision_results.method`, `dialogue_results.outcome`, `trace[*].{speaker,action}`. Un test de non-régression les épingle.
- **`dung_frameworks.name`** : l'issue demandait de trancher. Les **dix** sites d'appel le construisent depuis un vocabulaire fixe (`aba_preferred`, `setaf_grounded`, `social_af`, `dung_arbitration`, `verification_<sem>`, `delp_analysis`…). Le verdict firsthand de #1271 tient ⇒ **laissé intact**. C'est le scrubber du bundle, qui le remplace au-delà de 20 caractères, qui sur-scrubbe — pas celui-ci.
- **Pas de passe attrape-tout récursive.** Effacer « toute chaîne longue » détruirait les identifiants, méthodes et topologies d'extension que le contrat garantit ; le premier à en avoir besoin la désactiverait.

## Le balayage systématique (item 4 de la DoD) — le vrai livrable

Un marqueur **unique** planté dans chaque argument de type chaîne de **chaque** writer, état sérialisé par le vrai `get_state_snapshot()`, sortie parcourue pour retrouver chaque survivant **avec son chemin** :

```
avant : planted=60  reached_snapshot=57  survived_sanitize=33
après : planted=60  reached_snapshot=57  survived_sanitize=20
```

Les 13 tués sont exactement les sous-clés du tableau ci-dessus. Les 20 restants sont classés : étiquettes structurelles (à garder), et trois cas explicitement **non tranchés**, désormais écrits dans la docstring avec leur raison — `workflow_results` (dict libre, demande une politique et non une entrée de table), `formal_synthesis_reports[*].phase_results.*.formulas` (symbolique, mais Track 2 rend les symboles lisibles — c'est pourquoi `variables` EST opacifié : il faut lire le producteur), `extracts[*].name` et `semantic_index_refs[*].document_id` (déclarés comme des noms, mais structurels dans tous les artefacts mesurés et utilisés comme clés de jointure — les opacifier échangerait une fuite hypothétique contre une casse certaine).

La docstring énonce maintenant la limite du modèle en liste d'autorisation : **un conteneur absent de toutes les tables traverse intact**, donc ajouter un conteneur d'état n'est pas neutre. C'est ce non-dit qui a produit le trou.

## Falsifiabilité — substitution vérifiée, pas supposée

19 tests, état construit par les **vrais writers** et sérialisé par le **vrai** `get_state_snapshot()`. Une fixture littérale ne peut rien prouver ici : elle fournirait au garde la forme `dict` qu'aucun writer n'émet, et le test s'accorderait avec lui-même — c'est exactement ce qui a laissé le défaut dormir. La chaîne plantée ne contient aucun nom de la liste d'entités figée, pour que la mesure porte sur la protection **par forme**.

Revert chirurgical du seul fichier de production, tests inchangés : **12 KILL / 8 SPARE**, kill-sets disjoints par construction.

| Rôle | Tests | Revert |
|---|---|---|
| Le défaut | 7 paramétrés (claim text) + map d'acceptation + trace de dialogue + échanges de débat + topologie bipolaire + rien-ne-survit | **KILL** ×12 |
| Prémisse (7 conteneurs en forme de liste, Dung en dict) | `test_writers_emit_list_shaped_containers` | SPARE |
| Anti-pendule (étiquettes structurelles) | `test_structural_labels_not_over_scrubbed` | SPARE |

Le garde de prémisse est là pour un motif précis : si un refactor futur unifie les formes, il échoue **le premier** et le dit, au lieu de laisser une passe gardée par le type re-couvrir silencieusement une partie des conteneurs.

⚠️ `test_bipolar_support_topology_preserved` a d'abord **survécu** au revert : sur entrée non scrubbée, `supports[0][0]` et `arguments[0]` sont tous deux le texte brut, donc l'identité tenait trivialement. Corrigé en épinglant d'abord la non-vacuité (`arguments[0] != NL`), puis la relation.

## Portée — mesurée, et non gonflée

Sur les artefacts réels dont je dispose, ces sept conteneurs sont **vides**. **Aucune fuite constatée.** Ce qui est établi : un garde qui se déclare unique couvrait une fraction de ce qu'il annonce.

body:
## Problem

Every DataSet page in v2 renders without a License row, e.g.
https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?id=Berg2025

The licence is in the KB — `(:DataSet {short_form:'Berg2025'})-[:has_license]->(:License {short_form:'VFBlicense_CC_BY_4_0'})` — and it shows correctly in the `AllDatasets` results table. It is lost in term-info serialisation.

## Cause

`QueryLibrary.dataset_term_info` (VFB_json_schema) uses the `license()` clause, so a dataset's licence comes back in `license`. Images and templates use `dataSet_license()` and come back in `dataset_license`.

`term_info_parse_object` only ever read `dataset_license`, so DataSet terms serialised as `"Licenses": {}`. Downstream, `VFBProcessTermInfoVFBqueryJson.licenseList()` builds the Source + License block from `Licenses{}` alone, so with an empty dict no License row is added.

The fallback exists everywhere else — `term_info_queries.VFBTerm.get_license()` has `elif self.license:`, and the legacy `VFBProcessTermInfoJson.getLicense()` has the same `else if`. Only this serialiser lost it, so the row disappeared when v2 moved onto the VFBquery term-info path.

## Fix

Add the missing branch. `source`/`source_iri` are left empty: the dataset is its own source, and an empty source stops the panel rendering a Source row that links back to the page you are already on. No Java or client change needed — the `License` slot is already in `VFBMain.js`'s ordered field list.

## Verification

Parsed against live SOLR after the change:

| Dataset | Licence |
|---|---|
| Berg2025 | CC-BY 4.0 |
| Bates2025 | CC-BY 4.0 |
| Dorkenwald2023 | CC-BY-NC 4.0 |
| Cachero2010 | CC-BY-SA 4.0 |

Three tests added to `test_term_info_parity.py` as Gap E, alongside the gaps this serialiser has already been reconciled against. The two dataset tests fail on `main` and pass here; the third asserts the `dataset_license` path is unchanged (JRC2018U keeps both its licence and its source attribution).

Note: `test_individual_synonyms_present` in that file already fails on `main` and is untouched by this change.

author: posthog-eu[bot]
body:
## Problem

- Opening an event from the homepage list silently does nothing when a click lands mid-reflow — the product's single most important interaction, observed failing twice in one 8-minute session with **no `$autocapture`, `$pageview`, or `$dead_click`** emitted (the click was never dispatched, so frustration metrics undercount it).
- `visibleEvents` filters events through `isEventMostlyElapsed(...)`, which reads `now.value` — a global `Date` reassigned by a `setInterval(…, 1000)`. Once a second the keyed grid re-evaluates and any event crossing the 30%-elapsed threshold drops out, shifting every card below it upward. Between mousedown and mouseup, the browser then fires no `click`.
- `EventCard` compounds it: the `isPast`/`isOngoing` badges re-derive from the same ticker (a toggling badge changes card height), and `handleClick` calls `e.preventDefault()` **unconditionally**, so a failed JS path leaves no native `href` fallback.
- Position-dependent, not event-specific — any visitor scrolling the list can hit it.

## Changes

| Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| List re-filters every second | Filter against a **load-time snapshot** (`filterReferenceTime`) instead of the ticker — the grid no longer reshuffles under the pointer |
| Badges re-derive every second and change card height | Derive `isPast`/`isOngoing` from a **mount-time snapshot** so a badge can't appear/disappear mid-click |
| `preventDefault()` swallows every click | Only suppress native nav **after** the dialog opens, and leave modifier / non-primary clicks to the browser — a failed JS path degrades to the plain `<a href>` |
| Ticker now unused | Removed `src/lib/now.svelte.ts` (its only two importers are gone) |

## Risk / verification

- Trade-off: the elapsed-event filter and the "Vorbei"/"Läuft" badges now reflect state at page load rather than ticking live. Filtering upcoming events is a nicety, and freezing it is what keeps the list stable under the cursor.
- `now` was imported only in these two files (confirmed by grep); removing the module is safe.
- `svelte-check` reports no errors in the changed files. The app needs Supabase/S3/Telegram credentials and a populated DB to boot, which aren't available in this sandbox, so a live recording of the list wasn't possible — but the fix is structural: every reactive dependency on the per-second clock is removed, so nothing re-derives on a timer. There is no runtime state a recording would reveal differently.

## Agent context

Considered a coarse recompute interval instead of a snapshot; rejected because it still reshuffles the list occasionally under the cursor. The load-time snapshot eliminates the symptom entirely.

## Summary

- Three dual-role (`Roles(Trainer, Nutritionist)`) endpoints gated client data on
  `ClientProfessionalLink.IsActive` alone and returned **both** the nutrition and the
  training domain in one response. They now read the two capability flags off the link
  entity they already load: **neither flag → 403**, **one flag → only that domain**,
  **both flags → unchanged**.
- `ListClientPlans` and `GetClientTimeline` filter merged item lists — and do so by
  *not querying* the ungranted domain's collections at all, rather than filtering after
  the fact. `GetClientDashboard` substitutes the caller-entitled value into the existing
  `CompliancePercent` wire field and derives the `CurrentStreak` discipline from the flags.
- Both list responses now carry the caller's `canViewNutritionPlans` /
  `canViewTrainingPlans`, so the portal can distinguish "nothing exists" from
  "not permitted". `GetClientDashboardResponse` already carried them.
- Purely additive on the wire — no field renamed or invented, no `regen-api`, no EF
  migration, no change to `ProfessionalAuthHelper` / `NutritionAuthHelper` (that
  unification is #914).

## Related issue

Fixes #916

## Scope

backend

## Per-endpoint verdict table (AC1)

Audit surface: every endpoint under `Features/` that queries
`db.ClientProfessionalLinks` **and** returns per-client data spanning both the
nutrition and the training domain. 39 feature files query the link table; 11 touch
both domains. Independently re-derived at review time (grep of `Features/` for files
referencing `NutritionPlans|MealLogs|CalculateComplianceAsync` **and**
`TrainingPlans|SessionExecutions|PersonalRecords` **and** `ClientProfessionalLinks`,
plus `GetClientVerdict`, which reaches both domains indirectly via
`ClientVerdictService`) — same 11, no missed needs-fix endpoint.

| Endpoint | Verdict | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `Trainers/ListClientPlans/ListClientPlansEndpoint.cs` | ❌ Needs fix — **fixed in this PR** | Confirmed defect. `IsActive`-only check; returned nutrition plans + compliance alongside training plans, `SessionExecution`s and `PersonalRecord`s. Split into `LoadNutritionItemsAsync` / `LoadTrainingItemsAsync`, each behind its flag. |
| `Trainers/GetClientTimeline/GetClientTimelineEndpoint.cs` | ❌ Needs fix — **fixed in this PR** | Identical defect shape. Five of eight entry types are now domain-gated; three stay dual-readable (below). |
| `Trainers/GetClientDashboard/GetClientDashboardEndpoint.cs` | ❌ Needs fix — **fixed in this PR** | `CompliancePercent` is the *combined* weighted figure per `IComplianceService`; returning it to a single-flag caller leaks the other domain's adherence by inference. Now substitutes `NutritionCompliancePercent` / `TrainingCompliancePercent`, and passes the derived `ComplianceDiscipline` to `CalculateStreakAsync`. |
| `Trainers/GetClientVerdict/GetClientVerdictEndpoint.cs` | ⏸️ **Deferred — tracked by #919** | Its `Verdict` is a scalar blended from nutrition compliance, weight signals and training frequency (`ClientVerdictService.ComputeVerdict`). A scalar computed from data the caller may not see cannot be filtered — returning it to a partial-access caller leaks the hidden domain *by inference*. Needs the reduce / suppress / flag-as-partial decision #919 exists to settle. Note for #919: `PrCountThisMonth` (line 102) is returned unconditionally, unlike the plan-gated compliance and frequency fields — a raw training-domain value. |
| `Trainers/GetDashboardSummary/GetDashboardSummaryEndpoint.cs` | ⏸️ **Deferred — tracked by #919** | Aggregates across *all* of the professional's links and returns cross-client statistics, not per-client detail. Partitioning aggregate counters is a separate design problem with its own contract question; grouped with `GetClientVerdict` under one decision. |
| `Trainers/GetClientProgress/GetClientProgressEndpoint.cs` | ✅ **Dual-readable by design** | Already resolved by #903 (PR #915): gates on `ProfessionalAuthHelper.HasAnyPlanAccessAsync`, the sanctioned "either flag" primitive. This is the precedent the three fixes above follow; not re-listed as suspect. |
| `ClientMeasurements/GetClientMeasurements/GetClientMeasurementsEndpoint.cs` | ✅ **Dual-readable by design** | Gates on `IsActive` alone (line 70) and returns body measurements only. Bodyweight is core training data *and* core nutrition data; nutrition-gating it would break a legitimate trainer read. Same classification applied to the timeline's standalone `measurement` entries. |
| `WeeklyCheckIns/PutOverride/PutOverrideEndpoint.cs` | ✅ **Not a leak** | Keys the row on `ProfessionalUserId == caller` (line 87) — the caller only ever writes their own row and the endpoint returns no client domain data. Capability mismatch on a self-scoped write is a different bug class. |
| `WeeklyCheckIns/DeleteOverride/DeleteOverrideEndpoint.cs` | ✅ **Not a leak** | Same self-scoped shape (`ProfessionalUserId == caller`, line 91). |

Remaining six of the 11 cross-domain link-querying files are write or self-scoped and
return no per-client cross-domain read data, so they need no verdict row of their own:
`Auth/AcceptInvitation`, `Client/Invites/Accept/AcceptClientInvite`,
`PhotoDiaryRequests/CreateRequest`, `Trainers/ClientRequests/AcceptClientRequest`,
`Trainers/CreateCollaboration`, `Users/GetProfile`.
`WorkoutLogs/UpdateWorkout` also queries the link table but is `Roles(Client)` — not a
professional read path at all.

### Timeline entry-type classification

The copy-paste trap this issue circled for three review rounds: classify a datum by the
**item it is attached to**, not by its intrinsic domain.

| Entry type | Gate |
|---|---|
| `meal_day` | `CanViewNutritionPlans` |
| `nutrition_plan_published` | `CanViewNutritionPlans` |
| `workout` | `CanViewTrainingPlans` |
| `training_plan_published` | `CanViewTrainingPlans` |
| `personal_record` | `CanViewTrainingPlans` |
| `measurement` | ungated — standalone dual-readable entry |
| `questionnaire` | ungated — standalone dual-readable entry |
| `linked` | ungated — standalone dual-readable entry |

Contrast with `ListClientPlans`, where body measurements are *not* independently gated:
there they only feed `WeightDeltaKg` on a nutrition plan item, so they disappear with

**1. Status-code inconsistency this PR creates.** For an active link carrying neither
capability flag, these three endpoints now return **403**, while
`GetClientProgressEndpoint.cs:57-64` returns **404** for the equivalent condition

defensible (403 = "you exist but may not"; 404 = don't confirm the client exists). This

body:
Replaces the DD Map page, which held two external link cards, with a map of the Deep Desert point-of-interest layout for each of the 12 Coriolis world seeds.

### What it does

- **Seed selector, 0–11.** Pick a seed and the map redraws with that layout's caves, wrecks, testing stations, taxis, titanium and stravidium nodes, and large spice fields.
- **Opens on the live seed.** On load the page jumps to whichever seed the server is actually running and marks it in the selector.
- **Legend doubles as a filter.** Click a type to hide or show it; the header count tracks the visible subset.
- **Per-seed detail** — large spice sectors, POI count, capture date, and a note where one applies.

### Reading the live seed

No backend change was needed. `world_map_reset_seed` carries two naming schemes: partition names (`DeepDesert_1`) are what an admin *asked for*, friendly names (`DeepDesert`) are what the game *wrote back* after loading the map. The friendly row is the truth, so the page prefers it and falls back to the partition row. Both already come from the existing coriolis seeds endpoint.

### Why it draws client-side

The map is SVG rendered from a ~68 KB JSON payload rather than twelve baked PNGs, which would have added ~12 MB to the installer. It also makes the legend usable as a filter and gives every POI a hover label. Row A is the densest row on every seed, so its icons draw at half size to stop neighbouring pairs overlapping.

### Honesty about the data

The layout data was compiled from publicly archived community sources, not read from the user's server. A card on the page states that plainly and asks for corrections.

Certainty also varies per seed, so rather than one blanket caveat that dilutes everything, each seed carries a reliability and an optional note and is flagged in place. Two seeds are flagged:

| Seed | Why |
|---|---|
| 7 | Incomplete transcription. Records no titanium or stravidium mega nodes, though every other layout has at least one of each, and its sub-cell positions are placeholders rather than measured — only 2 distinct values across 26 POIs. |
| 10 | Matched only 2 of the 6 large-spice sectors on record for that seed, and its POI layout is 98.8% identical to seed 5 where any other pair shares ~22%. The layout is a real capture; the seed number attached to it is not well evidenced. |

**Seed 0 was corrected.** Its only captures date from July 2025, when the source over-reported mega nodes and stacked titanium and stravidium on the same sectors — 12 markers across 8 sectors, against 2–4 for every other seed. A later capture of a different layout shows the same pathology and drops exactly those stacked sectors when re-captured, which confirms it as a source-side artifact rather than real data. Seed 0 now carries four mega nodes and five caves, matching a reference map.

### Icons

All markers use the flat icon set so the map reads uniformly at any zoom. The titanium and stravidium node art from that set carries a dark backdrop baked into its outline path that only works against a near-black UI — on sand it covers ~60% of the icon. The ore is lifted out of that art and set on a diamond plate matching the spice marker instead. Taxi has no equivalent in the set and keeps its PNG.

### Also

- adds `resolveJsonModule` so the payload can be imported directly
- keeps `/dd-map` working and adds `/wick-maps`
- refreshes the bug report template for the renamed surface, including a dedicated option for wrong or missing layout data

### Verification

- `npm run build` (tsc + vite) clean
- Exercised in a browser: all 12 seeds render, every marker resolves, no broken assets, legend filter and seed switching both behave, and the low-confidence badge plus note appear on seeds 7 and 10

body:
## Problem

`getLanguageForFile` in the repo-map file classifier computes the extension as `filePath.substring(filePath.lastIndexOf('.'))` and looks it up in the plain `SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS` object with a `?? null` guard.

For a path with **no dot**, `lastIndexOf('.')` returns `-1` and `substring(-1)` clamps to `substring(0)` — so the whole filename becomes the lookup key. Two consequences:

1. **Extensionless files are misclassified**: the entire name is matched against the extension table instead of yielding "no extension".
2. **Prototype-member bypass**: a repo-root file named after an `Object.prototype` member (`constructor`, `__proto__`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`, …) resolves `SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS['constructor']` to the inherited member (truthy), which slips past `?? null`. `isSupportedFile` then returns `true` and `getLanguageForFile` hands back a `Function`/`Object.prototype` value cast as a `SupportedLanguage`, so the file enters the repo-map candidate set / pagerank graph with a bogus language. The file paths come from `git ls-files` / directory walk, so the key is repo-controlled.

Same class as the earlier diff `FILENAME_LANGS` fix; this is a different, still-bare site.

## Fix

Return `null` when there is no dot (no extension to match), and gate the lookup on `Object.hasOwn` — mirroring `resolveOutputStyle`'s own-property guard.

## Tests

New `gitFiles.test.ts`: supported/unsupported extensions, extensionless files (`Makefile`, `LICENSE`) → null, and prototype-member filenames → null (the last fails without the fix). 37 pass across the repo-map suite, typecheck clean.

body:
Un-stacks @IronLad123's #109, which could not merge: it sat on #107 and #108 and carried all three commits.

The rule changes are theirs and their test is applied as written. Closes #87.

## What was wrong

`\bPingRequest\w*` matched any identifier *starting* with the SDK name:

| identifier | rule | real MCP? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PingRequester` | R011 | no |
| `SetLevelRequesterFactory` | R012 | no |
| `InitializeRequesterHelper` | R009 | no |
| `CreateMessageRequestBuilder` | R007 | no |

## Extended past their branch in one place

`main` has since grown a **separate TypeScript pattern** in each of these four rules (`TS_PING_CODE_RX`, `TS_SET_LEVEL_CODE_RX`, and the TS arms in R007/R009). Those are a second set of `\w*` sites their branch predates.

Bounding only the Python half would have left the identical false positive live for every TypeScript project — which is most MCP servers, and the reason #87 was filed. Both halves are bounded here.

## Verified

18 false-positive and 18 true-positive cases, each in both `.py` and `.ts`:

- **every FP now silent** — `PingRequester`, `PingRequesterFactory`, `SetLevelRequesterFactory`, `SetLevelRequestBuilder`, `InitializeRequesterHelper`, `InitializeResultParser`, `CreateMessageRequestBuilder`, `CreateMessageResultFormatter`
- **every real SDK name still caught** — `PingRequestSchema`, `PingRequest`, `SetLevelRequestSchema`, `SetLevelRequestParams`, `InitializeRequestSchema`, `InitializeResult`, `InitializedNotificationSchema`, `CreateMessageRequestSchema`, `CreateMessageResult`

Pinned as parametrized tests so both directions stay covered.

## Closes an asymmetry we had been living with

R009, R011 and R012's **fixers** already bounded their own patterns, deliberately, while the rules did not — so `check` reported lines that `fix` then declined to touch, and the CHANGELOG said so in as many words. Rule and fixer now agree:

```
R011 fixer on 'helper = PingRequester()': changed=False
R012 fixer on 's = SetLevelRequesterFactory()': changed=False
R009 fixer on 'helper = InitializeRequesterHelper()': changed=False
```

**509 tests pass.**

#107, #108 and #110 remain open and still stacked; this only removes #109 from underneath them.
